pi_question: is this consistent with a pareto distribution?
short_answer: Partly. A pure Pareto over the whole range is rejected (p = 0.02). Restricted to fields of 2 or more detections it is not rejected (p = 0.13-0.38), with exponent alpha = 1.83. That tail is 40% of fields but 93% of all detections, so for the purpose the panel is making - that a few fields dominate any raw count - Pareto is a fair description.
method: Discrete (zeta) power law fitted by maximum likelihood, with the Clauset, Shalizi & Newman goodness-of-fit test: 400-1000 synthetic datasets drawn from the fitted law, each refitted, and p taken as the fraction whose KS distance equals or exceeds the observed. p > 0.1 means the power law cannot be rejected. An independent MLE written here reproduces the powerlaw package's alpha to three decimals (1.833).

full_range.why: the failure is at the small end: 817 singletons observed against 785 expected, with a deficit at sizes 4-5 (46 vs 56 and 28 vs 37). Singleton fields are exactly where detection completeness and the linking distance bite, so this is as likely to be a property of the catalog as of the hollows.

non_monotonic_caveat: p drops below 0.1 again for xmin between 10 and 30 and rises at 50. Those samples are 44-124 fields, where the KS test has little power and p is unstable. This is small-sample noise, not evidence of a second regime.

model_comparison_on_the_tail.vs_exponential: R = +6.92, p < 1e-4, power law strongly favored
model_comparison_on_the_tail.vs_truncated_power_law: R = -1.55, p = 0.150, not distinguishable (lambda = 4e-4, i.e. no detectable exponential cutoff)
model_comparison_on_the_tail.vs_lognormal: R = -2.08, p = 0.038 nominally favors lognormal, BUT the fitted lognormal is degenerate (mu = -980, sigma = 34.6), so this comparison is not usable. Reported here rather than quoted as evidence either way.

exponent_depends_on_the_linking_distance.note: alpha falls steadily from 1.97 to 1.70 across the calibrated 16-50 km plateau, so the exponent is not a parameter-free property of the hollow population. Quote it as alpha ~ 1.8 with the linking distance stated, never as a bare number.

concentration.note: the classic '80/20' Pareto statement would be 80%; here the top 20% of fields hold 87% of detections, i.e. slightly more concentrated than the folk version.

relation_to_bickel: Bickel et al. 2025 report that the hollow DIAMETER size-frequency distribution follows a power law with exponent 1.4-1.5. That is a different quantity - the size of an individual hollow, not the number of detections grouped into a field - so the two exponents should not be compared directly.
size_repeatability_note: the pooled log-size sd of 0.466 is inflated by the merged-field tail; the MAD-based 0.294 (a factor 1.34) is the appropriate per-hollow measurement error
